2609.26489.title: Calibration as a First-Class Criterion in LLM Evaluation
2609.26489.paper_summary: Calibration of language models -- the alignment between expressed or implicit confidence and empirical correctness -- is a well-studied subfield within NLP. Methods to measure it already exist. The problem is adoption: outside this subfield, NLP research regularly introduces new models, datasets, and benchmarks without checking whether the model's confidence scores are meaningful. We argue that this adoption gap is a major obstacle to trustworthy LLM evaluation. Miscalibration causes problems in two distinct areas: at deployment, where overconfident mistakes cause real harm, and inside the research pipeline, where methods like LLM-as-a-judge, synthetic data generation, and active learning rely on calibrated confidence without verifying it. Standard calibration metrics only require two inputs per example: a confidence score and a correctness judgment. Most benchmarks in use today already provide both, meaning calibration can be reported immediately. For open-ended generation, however, defining these two inputs is still an open challenge. We argue that each NLP subfield should pair its main performance metric with a calibration score and call for treating calibration as an essential property of every model rather than a niche topic.
2609.26489.paper_summary_zh: 語言模型的校準——表達或隱含的信心與實證正確性之間的對齊——是自然語言處理(NLP)中一個研究成熟的子領域。<lb/>目前已經存在測量它的方法。<lb/>問題在於採用：在這個子領域之外，NLP研究經常引入新的模型、數據集和基準，而不檢查模型的信心分數是否有意義。<lb/>我們認為這一採用差距是可信賴的大型語言模型(LLM)評估的一個主要障礙。<lb/>錯誤校準在兩個不同的領域造成問題：在部署階段，過度自信的錯誤會造成實際傷害；在研究流程中，像LLM作為評判者、合成數據生成和主動學習等方法依賴於校準的信心而不進行驗證。<lb/>標準的校準指標每個例子只需要兩個輸入：一個信心分數和一個正確性判斷。<lb/>目前使用的大多數基準已經提供了這兩者，這意味著校準可以立即報告。<lb/>然而，對於開放式生成，定義這兩個輸入仍然是一個未解的挑戰。<lb/>我們認為每個NLP子領域應該將其主要性能指標與校準分數配對，並呼籲將校準視為每個模型的基本屬性，而不是一個小眾主題。
